note: Two batches of VANISHED entries were written on 2026-09-03 and neither was a data restatement. (1) A rate-limited Yahoo sweep failed every retry for CRWD (round2) and XOM (round3); 52 fills across three books dropped out of the recomputation and returned intact on the re-run, logged here as RETURNED. tracker/round2.py now refuses to score a round at all when a symbol cannot be priced, so an outage can no longer rewrite the record. (2) The fill identity was changed so a perp leg carries its kind and leverage: Opus Value held BTC-USD spot and at 2x on the same day and the two collapsed into one id, leaving the leveraged leg unmonitored. 12 perp fills were re-keyed, so their old ids read as vanished and the same fills were appended under the new ids. No position changed and no NAV changed.

note:
The VANISHED and PRICE_RESTATED entries written on 2026-09-09 were caused by a CORRECTION IN THIS ENGINE, not by the data source restating anything. The journal's standard wording ('History was rewritten by a data restatement, not by a decision') is wrong for this batch and this note is the correction of record.

Yahoo stamps a daily bar with its START. Crypto bars start at 00:00 UTC, so the bar stamped day D closes at 00:00 UTC on D+1 - 20:00 in New York on D, four hours after that day's equity close, and therefore the bar belonging to session D. fetch() had been converting every symbol's timestamps to a New York date, which moves each crypto bar back to 20:00 the previous evening and files it one day EARLY. Every crypto mark in the experiment was one day out of step with the equities in the same book, and every crypto stop and take-profit was evaluated against the wrong day's close. It also silently disabled the guard that drops the live in-progress bar, because that guard compared a New York-dated index against a UTC date. Crypto is now dated by its UTC day.

What changed: every crypto standing order moved forward exactly one day - 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-19 - which is the same one-day lag observed on 2026-08-20, when five crypto orders appeared to fire late. That was treated at the time as a live-bar problem and only the symptom was fixed. One book changed more than by a day: Sonnet dividend growth and income lost a 2026-08-07 SOL-USD stop and gained a 2026-07-22 ETH-USD stop, because corrected prices changed which of its orders triggered first and the rest of the book followed. Across both rounds 30 of 75 books changed NAV, most by a few dollars, two by 17.13 and 8.10.

Separately, the reported date moved back to 2026-09-08. A crypto UTC day only settles at 00:00 UTC, after this 21:35 UTC refresh, so at run time the 2026-09-09 session could be priced for equities but not for crypto. The engine now reports the last session at which every held symbol has settled rather than marking part of a book against a bar that is still moving. The 2026-09-09 BABA stop that vanished here is not lost; it re-appears once that session is fully priced.
